title: Python Agent Migration Phase 3: Port Agent Engine, Turn Queue, Plans, Memory, and SSE Streaming

sections.what: Port agent-engine.ts, turn-queue.ts, simultaneous.ts, plan-manager.ts, memory-manager.ts, involuntary.ts, object-responder.ts, and threat-detector.ts into engine/agent/, streaming tokens and turn events over SSE (/api/agent/stream) while HumanTurnComposer submits human turns via POST /api/agent/human-turn.
sections.why: Running the turn loop and LLM execution on the Python server enables true headless LLM playtests and soaks via pytest/CLI, eliminates browser-vs-server state sync bugs, and keeps the browser strictly as a thin UI.
sections.how:
1. Port turn queue, simultaneous round coordinator, think/act/react loop, plan grounding/tracking, memory reconsolidation, and involuntary triggers into engine/agent/.
2. Add SSE endpoint /api/agent/stream for live token/event streaming and POST /api/agent/human-turn for HumanTurnComposer.
3. Thin out static/js/agent-engine.ts into an SSE subscriber + UI bridge and verify live play + headless pytest multi-actor turns.
sections.verify: Headless pytest multi-actor turn loop runs without a browser, and live Play Mode streams tokens and pauses cleanly for HumanTurnComposer.

acceptance.text: Python engine/agent/ runs full multi-actor think/act/react turns headlessly.
SSE stream delivers live tokens and turn events to the browser UI.
HumanTurnComposer submits human turns cleanly through the Python turn queue.

custom.browser_ui: In Play Mode, verify streaming tokens, Turn Order panel, event-stream up-next strip, and HumanTurnComposer pause/resume/reroll work smoothly over SSE with zero console errors.
